references.text: John quoted directly from Psalm 41:10 to show that the betrayal by a close friend was predicted in Scripture. Both texts use the image of one who eats my bread and lifts his heel against me.

In his high priestly prayer, Jesus confirms that he knew whom he had chosen and that none of them were lost except 'the son of destruction,' so that Scripture might be fulfilled. This mirrors the statement in 13:18 that he knows whom he has chosen.
Earlier in the Gospel, Jesus points out that he has chosen the twelve, but that one of them is a devil. This prepares the theme of election and betrayal which is central to 13:18.

Here Jesus again refers to the fulfillment of Scripture by quoting Psalm 35:19, which speaks of hatred from friends without cause. This is a parallel theme to 13:18, even though it is a different quotation showing that the betrayal was predicted.
